Internal: a model's predictors, checked and made ready to fit

Source: R/models.R
dot-jst_model_iv_loop.Rd

The name arguments checked against the predictors (the outcome left out of numeric = and count =, and a note when categorical = names it; a name that is not a predictor stops; a variable in two of them stops), then each predictor: a per-call override (numeric =, count =, categorical =), a computed term left as it is, else the classifier – categorical by intent gets an in-flight dummy registration, otherwise it enters as numbers, with the dichotomy note or one seems-categorical warning for all – and the in-flight registrations expanded into dummy columns. jlm() and jlogistic() each held the loop and the expansion (Session 386, the twin build); the checks were jlm()'s alone, and jlogistic() gains them (D2, the S385 drift finding).

Usage

.jst_model_iv_loop(
  data,
  formula,
  model_vars,
  dv_name,
  iv_names,
  numeric,
  categorical,
  count,
  dummy_coef_names,
  expanded_originals,
  resolved,
  pipeline,
  data_in,
  .jst_data_name,
  .jst_data_kind,
  .jst_default_used,
  formula_typed,
  auto_ref_cats,
  auto_cat_regs,
  one_cat_in_call,
  seems_cat,
  fn,
  skip_absent
)

Arguments

data, formula, model_vars

The data, formula and its variables.

dv_name

Character(1): the outcome.

iv_names

Character: the predictors.

numeric, categorical, count

The name arguments, read.

dummy_coef_names, expanded_originals

jdummy()'s columns and the variables they replaced.

resolved

The transforms' resolution (its computed columns).

pipeline, data_in

The pipeline's result and the data before it.

.jst_data_name, .jst_data_kind, .jst_default_used, formula_typed

The data's name and kind, the default flag and the formula as typed.

auto_ref_cats, auto_cat_regs, one_cat_in_call, seems_cat

Their values so far.

fn

Character(1): the calling function.

skip_absent

Logical(1): pass over a predictor not in the data (jlogistic()'s guard).

Value

list(data, formula, model_vars, dummy_coef_names, auto_cat_regs, auto_ref_cats, one_cat_in_call, numeric, categorical, count).
